thresholds.note: Every threshold in this file is an authored score read from data/pool.json, not a percentile of anybody's population. A percentile moves when the population moves, so the target slides while somebody is chasing it, and a benchmark for improvement wants a number that sits still. Each one carries a `source` saying whether it was adopted verbatim from a published benchmark, reconciled between several, authored outright with a reason, or is still seeded - inherited from the percentile era and not yet given a source. npm run validate:thresholds re-derives the first two and counts the last.

boards.note: The boards no longer set the thresholds; they audit them. Each scenario carries `sanity.clears` - what share of that leaderboard meets each rank - which is how a threshold nobody can reach, or one everybody clears, gets caught now that no percentile guarantees it by construction.
